assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is a general, ligand-controlled method for forming aryl C-N bonds, now routine in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. Originality, clarity and breadth of impact are exceptional and fit the Nobel tradition of enabling synthetic tools.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the ligand-enabled, general catalytic amination that made the reaction practical. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a precursor, and the question of its credit is the main allocation issue; a two-person prize is the cleanest configuration.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of independent use at industrial scale; the field is stable and recognition is timely, with palladium cross-coupling already honored in 2010.
uncertainties: Treatment of Kosugi's precursor work relative to the Buchwald-Hartwig ligand-enabled reaction
Overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize may be judged as incremental by some members
My assessment rests on recalled knowledge, not independent verification of priority claims

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites became a leading photovoltaic absorber within a decade, with efficiencies rivaling silicon, and opened a large materials-chemistry research field of defect-tolerant semiconductors.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitized cell, Park delivered the solid-state cell with improved stability and efficiency, and Snaith demonstrated the meso-superstructured and planar thin-film device. Seok, Kanatzidis and Grätzel also contributed, so credit is crowded and a three-person cap forces hard choices.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency progress is well confirmed across many laboratories, but long-term operational stability and lead toxicity remain unresolved for deployment, so recognition could be seen as early for the technology yet timely for the science.
uncertainties: Crowded credit across six names
Commercial stability still unproven
Whether the prize should recognize the chemistry of the material or the device

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by synthesis transformed biology and medicine, reducing the cost of genome sequencing by orders of magnitude. It is a chemical invention built on reversible terminators, fluorescent labelling and surface-attached clonal clusters.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa chemistry, and Mayer's clustered-colony concept contributed to the platform. Rothberg (pyrosequencing arrays) and Ju (terminator chemistry) are also credited, so which technology line is recognized is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with two decades of universal use; recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Competing technology lines such as 454 pyrosequencing, terminator chemistry and Solexa
Fit to chemistry versus physiology or medicine
Commercial and company-related credit complicates allocation

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues reframes drug discovery by hijacking E3 ligases to destroy proteins, with chemically defined mechanisms and drugs in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced and developed the PROTAC concept, and Ciulli provided structure-guided design and VHL ligands. Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the target of thalidomide and the molecular glue mechanism, a separate part of the discovery that may require its own recognition.
assessment.maturity: Scientifically well confirmed and rapidly expanding, but clinical validation by approved drugs is still pending, so recognition could be premature.
uncertainties: Clinical validation incomplete
Compound discovery: PROTACs versus molecular glues and cereblon
Eight credited names, with several equally plausible subsets

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and molecular sieves, with organic structure-directing agents, new framework topologies and hierarchical and active-site control, underlies petrochemical refining and emission control. It is close to my own field, and structure determination of new zeolites, increasingly by 3D electron diffraction, was crucial to progress.
assessment.attribution: Corma (catalytic design and industrial zeolite catalysts), Davis (synthesis and design of molecular sieves) and Zones (organic structure-directing agents, SSZ materials at Chevron) are central. Yu and Tsapatsis are also credited, and the spread of contributions makes a sharply defined discovery hard.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation with major industrial impact; timing is ready, though the 2025 prize on porous frameworks may reduce appetite for another porous-materials award.
uncertainties: Diffuse discovery with no single decisive step
Possible overlap with recent MOF recognition
Potential personal bias from my own area

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The dye-sensitized nanocrystalline solar cell introduced mesoporous semiconductor photoelectrodes with molecular sensitizers, a lasting chemical approach to photovoltaics that seeded later perovskite and photoelectrochemical research.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 O'Regan and Grätzel paper is the defining contribution, and Grätzel led the field subsequently. Hagfeldt contributed to later mechanistic and device understanding but is less decisive.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and extensively confirmed, with continued relevance in indoor photovoltaics; recognition is sometimes judged late relative to the discovery.
uncertainties: Commercial impact more modest than expected
Whether Grätzel alone or together with O'Regan is appropriate
Grätzel also appears in the perovskite candidate, so the two could overlap

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base pair into another without double-strand breaks by combining deaminase chemistry with programmable DNA-binding proteins, and it is entering clinical use.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the design, with Komor developing the cytosine base editors and Gaudelli the adenine base editors; Nishida and Kondo reported a related early cytidine deaminase fusion, raising an allocation issue.
assessment.maturity: Very recent, with early clinical results strong but long-term safety and efficacy still to be established; recognition is possibly premature, especially after the 2020 prize for CRISPR.
uncertainties: Recency and clinical maturity
Closeness to the 2020 CRISPR prize
Priority of Nishida and Kondo versus Komor and Gaudelli

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Template-directed ordered mesoporous silica (M41S, MCM-41, SBA-15) extended porous-solid design beyond zeolite pore sizes and spawned a large field of ordered mesoporous materials. Structure characterization by electron microscopy and diffraction was important in establishing it.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck at Mobil discovered M41S, Ryoo developed ordered mesoporous carbons and related materials, and Stucky and Zhao developed SBA-15. Inagaki's independent FSM-16 work adds a priority question, and the six-name list does not map easily to a three-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Well established for three decades; applications are real but the practical impact is more modest than for zeolites, so it ranks lower.
uncertainties: Priority among Mobil, Inagaki and Stucky groups
Industrial impact more limited than the scientific influence
Limited three-laureate fit
